title: Locale-aware toast announcer and contrast token prototype review
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Goal: Validate a lightweight, production-ready pattern for toast notifications and contrast token mappings that work correctly across locales (including RTL), screen readers, and constrained density modes. This ticket covers a high-fidelity prototype review, accessibility test notes, and a short implementation spec for ENG to pick up. Key constraints: minimal bundle impact, no additional runtime i18n libs, compatibility with existing Console toast queueing and rollouts flow.
scope: Prototype and review live-announcement behavior, toast stacking semantics, aria-live politeness mode based on user action, locale-aware number/date display inside toasts, color token contrast mapping for compact and dense UI, and keyboard focus flow when toasts overlap rollouts modals or snackbars.
acceptance_criteria: ARIA announcements: critical error toasts use aria-live='assertive' with a single concise message; non-critical confirmations use aria-live='polite' and are deduped if same message arrives within 2s.
Screen reader UX: VoiceOver, NVDA, and JAWS read the important toast content exactly once when it appears; focus is not stolen from active modal unless the toast requires user interaction.
Locale formatting: numbers in toast body are rendered via Intl.NumberFormat(customerLocale) and respects compact notation (e.g., 1.2K) only when locale patterns indicate readability improvements.
RTL: toast placement and enter/exit animations flip correctly for RTL locales; live region semantics remain correct and unaffected by visual mirroring.

Contrast tokens: mapped token set meets WCAG 2.1 AA for normal text and 3.0 for large display text in the Cost and Rollouts mini-cards; design tokens documented as --color-toast-text, --color-toast-bg, --color-toast-border for each density and theme.

Keyboard flow: Escape closes non-persistent toasts; persistent toasts (that require action) trap focus to the toast until user dismisses or completes action; tab order is clearly defined and documented.
Perf/regression: Prototype must not increase initial CSS bundle by >4KB gz and not introduce runtime Intl polyfills.
Design handoff: Figma frames, motion specs, and annotated tokens are attached and linked in the ticket.
attachments: https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/ -- reference used to compute token deltas
comments: 2026-02-20 - Ava Rodriguez: Initial prototype uploaded to Figma. Focus: how announcements behave while user is in a rollouts modal. See 'Announcement Patterns' frame.

2026-02-22 - Diego Morales (ENG): Reviewed implementation constraints. Noted Intl.NumberFormat is available in hosted environments; ENG flagged older on-prem nodes might need polyfill. ENG impact estimate: 2 points for a guarded Intl use + 1 point for toast focus trap logic.
2026-02-24 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Customer signal from two enterprise accounts requesting clearer cost delta toasts (locale formatted) during canary rollouts. Marked as medium priority for this cycle.

2026-02-27 - Maya Chen: Updated Figma with two density variants (compact/dense) and color token overlays. Added token table mapping for AA/AAA thresholds and fallback values for low-contrast tokens in legacy themes.

2026-03-01 - Accessibility review by Jordan Ellis: Tested VoiceOver on macOS and NVDA on Windows. Findings: (1) assertive announcements sometimes interrupt reading of large, persistent modals; recommend using polite for non-blocking events and only assertive for blocking errors. (2) Screen reader users benefit from a visible 'View details' link inside toasts for complex messages so they can request verbose content explicitly.

2026-03-03 - Engineering comment by Diego Morales: We'll implement a per-toast 'politeness' flag and a global dedupe window. Requesting a short JSON schema for toast payloads (see attachments to follow). Also noted need for a feature flag for Intl polyfill on older Private deployments.

2026-03-05 - UX decision (Ava/Maya/Diego): Use aria-live='assertive' only for 'blocking' and 'action required' errors. All other toasts use aria-live='polite'. Add a data attribute data-toast-id to dedupe identical messages for 2s. Implement explicit 'aria-describedby' linking to the toast action where relevant.

2026-03-07 - Localization note by Igor Petrov (i18n): Confirmed RTL flip for animations is safe; suggested checking double-width digits in locales using Indic numerals; toasts should avoid hardcoded punctuation that doesn't localize well.

2026-03-09 - QA checklist added by Maya Chen: manual cross-browser checks (Chrome/Firefox/Safari), screen reader passes (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS), keyboard-only flow, RTL visual verification, contrast delta testing for light/dark and compact/dense tokens.

2026-03-10 - Maya Chen: Moving ticket to In Review. ENG stub PR created (see attachments). Next: ENG to implement guarded Intl usage and focus trap patterns; Design to approve token deltas after ENG theming layer exposes tokens. Follow-up ticket DES-73589 will audit chart scrubbers and live regions in the cost explorer after this ship.

Reviewer notes: Priya (PM) - please confirm acceptable fallback behavior for Private deployments that cannot ship Intl polyfill by release date; Jordan (A11y) - please re-run voiceover pass once ENG implements the politeness switch.
